```

1. Also OFFER to log in and continue — not just clean the message.
2. Do it as a **clone-specific precondition** (check session BEFORE the mirror lookup; if missing/expired, run `entire login` INLINE in the same process, then continue). Do NOT use a central main.go catch or re-exec.

## Part 1 — clean-message base (all control-plane commands)
`renderCoreError` (`cmd/entire/cli/corecmd.go:639-647`) is the single choke point for every control-plane command (org/project/repo/grant/mirror/clone via runCore→runCoreClient at corecmd.go:601-617). Design a change so that when the error chain contains `tokenmanager.ErrReauthRequired` or `auth.ErrNotLoggedIn`, it returns just the clean inner `reauthError.Error()` message (strip the noise). Note: must unwrap to the sentinel/`*reauthError`, NOT string-match the top-level message (two noise layers). ## Part 2 — clone precondition + inline login
In `newRepoCloneCmd` RunE (`cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone.go:78-180`), before `resolvePullablePlacements`/`runWithCore`, add a precondition that ensures a usable session. Investigate and specify:

a) **How to probe session validity cheaply.** The active-context token provider is built via `auth.NewRefreshingLoginProvider` (refresh.go:195). Calling the provider func triggers a refresh and returns either a token or a reauth error (ErrReauthRequired/ErrNotLoggedIn). Determine the cleanest way for the clone command to run this probe for the ACTIVE context (and consider: is there an existing "am I logged in / auth status" helper it should reuse instead? e.g. around `cmd/entire/cli/auth.go`, `authcmd.go`, `entireapi_client.go:48`, `api_client.go:35`). Report what `coreapi.New()` / the `activeCoreClient` seam (corecmd.go:564) actually does and whether the probe can piggyback on client construction.

b) **The `--cluster` path.** With `--cluster`, clone dials a DIFFERENT core/context via `runCoreForCluster`→`clusterCoreClient` (coreapi.NewForCluster). A session precondition there concerns a different context. Decide whether the precondition covers only the active-context path (the reported bug) or also `--cluster`, and how to keep it correct/simple. It's acceptable to scope the precondition to the active-context (no --cluster) path and let the --cluster path rely on the Part 1 clean-message fallback.

c) **Invoking `entire login` in-process.** Find the login command entry point (search for the login cobra command, likely `cmd/entire/cli/login*.go` or `auth/*login*`). Determine how to run it in-process so that AFTER it completes, a freshly-built token provider/client in the SAME process picks up the newly stored token (token store / keychain re-read). Confirm whether the token manager caches anything per-process that would make the continued command still see the old expired state (see refresh.go notes about the manager freezing settings / re-reading the store). Specify how to rebuild the client after login.

d) **Interactive gating + agent-safe fallback.** Only prompt+login when interactive: use `interactive.CanPromptInteractively()` (see CLAUDE.md 'Spawning subprocesses / TTY detection' section). When NOT interactive, the precondition must return the clean Part-1 message (so agents/CI see the hint and a non-zero exit) — never hang on a prompt. func ReauthMessage(err error) (string, bool) {

Not doing: a central main.go catch or re-exec (that's PR #1794's `cli_upgrade_required` shape — deliberately not reused here). This work is unrelated to the current `fix/local-repo-checkpoint-probe` branch and should land as its own PR branched off `main`.

// accessor for the unexported type — the cli package can't errors.As it, and

func ReauthMessage(err error) (string, bool) {

		return re.Error(), true
	}
	return "", false
